name: Broken-Wing Iron Condor
summary: An iron condor with unequal wing widths - the wing on the side you fear least is widened - to collect more credit or to skew where the loss lives.

legs.strike_rule: short put strike minus W_put (the NARROW wing if bias is bullish, e.g. $3)
short call strike plus W_call, where W_call > W_put (the WIDE wing), typically 2x the narrow wing

max_loss: (WIDER wing width - net credit) x 100 - the loss is asymmetric and lands on the wide-wing side
breakevens: lower BE = short put - credit; upper BE = short call + credit (same as a balanced IC; only the tail loss differs)

greeks.delta: slightly skewed away from the wide wing, typically -0.05 to -0.10 per 1-lot when the call wing is the wide one
greeks.theta: positive, slightly higher than a balanced IC for the same shorts

when_to_use: Same IV conditions as a standard iron condor, plus a mild directional lean: widen the wing on the side you consider less likely to be tested (bullish lean = wide call wing is wrong; widen the PUT wing only if you are bearish). Also used when one side's wing strikes are illiquid.
entry_rules: All standard iron condor entry filters apply (IVR >= 30, 30-60 DTE, no events, liquidity)
Wide wing width <= 3x the narrow wing width; beyond that the tail risk is not worth the extra credit
Net credit >= 30% of the WIDER wing width
Directional lean must be justified by a rule, not intuition: widen the call wing only when the 20-day SMA slope is negative, widen the put wing only when it is positive
management_rules: Extra rule: if the WIDE-wing side is tested (that short's delta >= 0.30), close the whole structure immediately rather than rolling - the asymmetric tail is the reason this trade exists and it is the one that hurts
If the NARROW-wing side is tested, roll that vertical out/away for a credit once, or close
exit_rules: Force-close the entire structure by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
Close immediately if any short goes ITM by > 0.25 x its own wing width, or a short delta >= 0.85, or short extrinsic < $0.10
Ex-dividend guard on the short call as per standard iron condor
assignment_risk: Same as an iron condor - both shorts assignable, wide wing gives no extra protection against assignment, only against unbounded loss.
liquidity_needs: Same as iron condor; the wide wing strike must still have OI >= 250 so it can be closed.
common_mistakes: Widening the wing on the side that actually trends; treating the extra credit as free; sizing off the narrow wing instead of the wide wing.
zero_dte_notes: Usable but the asymmetric tail plus 0DTE gamma is a bad combination unless the wide wing is on the statistically quieter side. Prefer the balanced iron condor intraday.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
